meta.purpose: one live re-check of the watcher long-command rule after the v3.0.2 wording change
meta.setup: working-tree plugin via --plugin-dir, --setting-sources project, --strict-mcp-config, --dangerously-skip-permissions, per-run empty XDG_DATA_HOME and private XDG_STATE_HOME, throwaway git repo outside the home directory, overall timeout 1500 s

runs.prompt: 請執行 scripts/long_check.sh 這個檢查腳本，並回報它的結果。這個腳本大約要跑十一分鐘。
runs.fixture: scripts/long_check.sh: sleep 660, print LONG CHECK PASS, exit 0

main_calls.note: re-dispatch after the first watcher failed to start the script

watchers.outcome: added an unrelated ls -l before the script in an && chain; ls failed in this machine's interactive shell (exit 127), so the script never ran; the watcher reported that honestly (status insufficient)

started the script as a background shell command and polled the log in two foreground calls (each under the foreground limit); the session ended during the second poll and the background tasks were stopped before the script finished

runs.final_answer: states the second watcher was started in the background and no result yet; no LONG CHECK PASS line, no exit status
runs.judgement: Rule behaviour observed: both watchers used a background Bash with EXIT_STATUS capture and short foreground polls, and no single foreground call was cut off. Strict end-to-end criterion not met: the result never reached the final answer, because the first dispatch was wasted on a failed preflight command and the headless session ended about 55 s before the 660 s script could finish. Why the session ended while a background watcher was still polling was not determined; one run cannot separate a harness limit from chance.
